speaker: King Sudarsana
title: Willpower versus passive fate
text: Nay! and faint not, idly sighing, 'Destiny is mightiest,' Sesamum holds oil in plenty, but it yieldeth none unpressed. Ah! it is the Coward's babble, 'Fortune taketh, Fortune gave;' Fortune! rate her like a master, and she serves thee like a slave. Twofold is the life we live in - Fate and Will together run: - Two wheels bear life's chariot onward - will it move on only one?
modern_interpretation: Do not despair or resign yourself to the idea that fate alone dictates your life. Just as sesame seeds contain oil but won't yield it unless pressed, your potential requires effort and action to be realized. It's a sign of weakness to constantly blame 'fortune' for your setbacks. Instead, assert your agency and master your circumstances, and you'll find that 'fortune' will work for you. Life progresses through a combination of destiny and your own willpower; you cannot expect to move forward relying solely on external forces without your active participation.
summary: This wisdom asserts that active effort and willpower are crucial for progress, refuting the passive acceptance of destiny or fortune as the sole determinant of one's life. It encourages taking charge of circumstances rather than succumbing to a victim mentality.
actionable_advice: Identify one area where you feel held back by external circumstances and commit to taking a small, deliberate action today to exert your will and influence the outcome.
embedding_ready_text: This profound wisdom from King Sudarsana in Hitopadesa, ID hitopadesa_effort_002, directly challenges the passivity of blaming 'Destiny' or 'Fortune' for one's lack of progress. It is a powerful antidote to feelings of resignation, helplessness, and inaction, explicitly labeling such thoughts as 'Coward's babble.' Through compelling analogies like sesame seeds yielding oil only when pressed, and life's chariot needing two wheels (Fate and Will), the text vehemently advocates for active effort, willpower, and personal agency. It urges individuals to master their circumstances and cultivate determination, courage, and resilience. This wisdom offers transformative guidance for overcoming procrastination, victim mentality, and low self-esteem, fostering a proactive mindset essential for self-growth, career advancement, and mental well-being by emphasizing that while destiny plays a part, conscious effort is non-negotiable for forward movement.
